Is there anything to prevent countries from using or threatening to use nuclear weapons against their own citizens?
Well, the citizens are where countries derive their power from. Nuking them would be a bad idea.

But since citizens reproduce without needing training (don't get me started!) the major thing to save is the infrastructure. Hence the "neutron bomb" idea, popular years ago, to take over countries by killing the people (resistance movement) but keeping their stuff (which will be relatively undamaged by firestorms and blast waves).

It's generally a bad idea to threaten/nuke your population directly. Just forces people to realize they're dead anyway if they don't do anything, so they might as well resist with everything they have. Now in saying that you could always use an attack as a false flag to achieve a goal. But to directly and openly admit you'd nuke your populous? Suicide. A violent horrible suicide at the hands of millions, including your closest supporters. Remember most people that run the show aren't willing to help murder their friends, family and loved ones. Although "just following orders" is a powerful excuse to weak minds...
But what about nuclear weapon equivalent to suicide bombers? Or do suicide bombers "just follow orders" as well?

Suicide bombers follow an ideology or do so for other reasons than just following orders. My reference was to the Nuremberg trials and how Nazi officers would claim they were just following orders to justify their slaughter of "undesirables". Good men can do horrible acts when an authority figure tells them too. In the eyes of the actor, if an authority figure says do something then the responsibility is on the authority figure, the actor is simply a cog. Humanity as a collective has proven several times that the excuse "just following orders" is not a valid defense when you know what you are doing is morally wrong, or illegal... but far too often individuals who are told from birth to respect authority will bow to its will when told too; simply because that is what they have always done.
Also, I beleive their families get paid well.
Nuclear Fallout is a bitch to clean.
That would be really silly, but sure they could do it if they wanted to kill/ destroy all of their power, money and resources.
If you kill your own people, then you have to power. Also, the soldiers that you are leading have families and property. Their loyalty to you will only good so far.
Why would you nuke your own population is the better question? There are only crazy answers to be found there.
One, no one believe the threat until you actually did it, and if you actually did nuke a city full of your own citizens the rest would rise up and tear them apart.
Anything tangible? No. You'd have to be a pretty awful leader to want to murder your populous and scorch your own land though.
Just the integrity of the military personnel directly in charge of the weapons, and the fear of the 2nd Amendment.

You might as well ask, "Is there anything to prevent countries from using or threatening to use (chemical | biological | conventional) weapons against their own citizens?"

Only the repercussions of doing so.

Sanity. Nuking your own population=a bunch of fallout on your own territory as the best case scenario.

If it went free-to-play, the player base would also skyrocket as well, which would be amazing for online play and matchmaking, as well as open up the option for a more notable e-sports scene.

At its core, Evolve is actually a great game and I love playing it, but it definitely isn't worth $60 (I paid $30) since it's essentially a multiplayer game, and the monetization method is absolutely appalling. I find it extremely hard to justify paying the amount of money the developers ask for a new character, or a new monster - it's actually insulting.

Brink.

I had really high hopes for it, but didn't and still don't like the idea of a competitive online campaign. Titanfall had the same problem. Additionally, in Brink, you could unlock all the weapons by simply doing the movement tutorials. This type of game gets a certain amount of carrot stick dynamic by having unlockable weapons determined by time played, and they took that out right from the start. Additionally there weren't enough maps or gametypes. It launched as a retail game for $40 dollars, it really needed some more time in the oven or a fifty percent price reduction so it could have launched as a really good Xbox Live Arcade or PSN title. The movement system was really cool, and giving different classes distinct objectives was also a really cool idea, but in the end it just didn't click.

I bet if Brink launched in today's gaming world, it'd be free to play with paid cosmetic items. The character creator and clothing was really cool and ahead of the times, but now everything that made it unique is old hat. The parkour style movement system, the shifting objectives, and yes, cosmetic stuff are in everything from Halo to CoD now.

Dead Island would be an excellent game, if only a few things were fixed.

  1. When the game came out it had some major bugs. Test your games damnit! Don't send out broken games.

  2. The level-up caps were pretty low, and it seemed way too hard to get new/improved abilities.

  3. Voice acting was awful. Very awful.

  4. There was no splitscreen local multiplayer. This sort of game, I feel, would benefit from that.

  5. Weapons broke so fast. It seemed rather unrealistic, just a way to keep your busy.

  6. Zombies are zombies, and they're dangerous, but this game exaggerated their qualities too much. Made them super monsters, and they would swarm, and sneak up on you. There was no mercy. It got pretty annoying, and repetitive.

  7. The story needed to be fixed up. There was just very little emotional attachment to the character. It was pretty cut and dry. The characters that you did like had a tendency to die.

  8. Your character felt so weak. As a player you had no qualities that really made you stick out from other people, other than your immunity. You felt rather sluggish. The stamina limits were annoying. Stamina, yes, but it should not get sapped away so fast, especially when a lot of the game involves running away.

  9. The fetch quests were a pain in the ass. If you have a fetch quest make it fun, and add to the story line. Decisions should count for something.

  10. There should have been more of a survival aspect, like collecting essential items, and strengthening your fortress, and that sort of thing. It's fundamental to a zombie game of this magnitude.

  11. More guns damnit. More weapons.

  12. Limited trunk space was a pain. I know it's unrealistic to be able to carry everything you want, but just let us. Or make it so that we can upgrade to eventually carry a shit load of stuff.
Dying Light fixed a lot of the game's problems, I'd suggest giving it a look if you haven't already. It added a pretty fun parkour system, too.
